description: This classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a comforting and nutritious staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. It features vibrant red lentils simmered with aromatic vegetables and traditional spices, creating a hearty yet light meal. Enjoy this flavorful and wholesome soup as a starter or a complete vegetarian dish, perfect for any season.

instructions.title: Prepare the Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and diced carrots. Saute for 8-10 minutes, or until the vegetables have softened and the onion is translucent, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic, ground cumin, and turmeric powder (if using). Cook for another 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant. Be careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Incorporate Lentils and Liquid
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the vegetables and spices. Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the soup simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend (Optional) and Season
instructions.text: For a smoother soup, use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup directly in the pot until desired consistency is reached. Alternatively, carefully transfer portions to a regular blender and blend, then return to the pot. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice, salt, and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasonings as needed.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. A drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and an additional lemon wedge can also be added for extra flavor and presentation. Serve immediately with warm pita bread or crusty bread.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of dried mint during the last few minutes of simmering, a common practice in Lebanese cooking.

article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East with a bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known affectionately as Adas. This humble yet profoundly flavorful soup is a staple in Lebanese homes, cherished for its comforting warmth, nourishing properties, and incredible simplicity. As a shining example within the vast array of Middle Eastern Soups and Stews, Adas transcends mere sustenance, offering a taste of tradition and a hug in a bowl, perfect for chilly evenings or a light, healthy meal any time of year.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a classic vegetarian dish celebrated across the Levant. "Adas" is simply the Arabic word for lentils, highlighting the star ingredient of this beloved soup. It's characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue, creamy texture (achieved by the natural breakdown of red lentils), and a bright, tangy finish from a generous squeeze of lemon juice. Unlike some more elaborate lentil soups, Adas keeps it elegantly simple: red lentils, basic aromatics like onion and garlic, a hint of cumin, and plenty of fresh lemon. This combination creates a remarkably complex flavor profile that is both deeply satisfying and refreshingly light. Often enjoyed during the colder months, as a comforting Iftar meal during Ramadan, or simply as a nutritious weeknight dinner, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a testament to the beauty of simple ingredients coming together to create something extraordinary. It’s naturally gluten-free and easily made vegan, making it a versatile option for many dietary preferences.

## Ingredients for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

The magic of this soup lies in its straightforward, wholesome ingredients. You likely have most of these in your pantry already!

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Choose split red lentils as they cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture.
*   **Onion:** One large yellow or white onion, finely chopped, forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** Several cloves, minced, add pungent depth.
*   **Olive Oil:** A good quality extra virgin olive oil is essential for sautéing and a final drizzle.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** Vegetable broth will add more flavor, but water works perfectly fine too, especially when combined with good seasoning.
*   **Cumin:** Ground cumin is the primary spice, imparting that unmistakable earthy, warm Middle Eastern flavor.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste, enhancing all the other flavors.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for brightness and balancing the earthy lentils. Do not skip this!
*   **Optional Garnishes:** Fresh cilantro or mint, a swirl of extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, crispy pita bread for dipping.

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Step-by-Step)

Creating a delicious bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is surprisingly simple. Follow these steps for a perfect batch every time:

1.  **Rinse the Lentils:** Place the red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse them thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, ensuring a clean flavor.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, or until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Stir in the rinsed lentils, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper. Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
4.  **Simmer:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially, and let the soup simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have broken down, creating a thick, creamy consistency. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional):** For an extra smooth soup, use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup directly in the pot. Alternatively, carefully transfer half of the soup to a regular blender (vent the lid to release steam!) and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. I prefer to leave some texture, so I only blend about half.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice. Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning as needed, adding more salt, pepper, cumin, or lemon juice to your preference.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish with a drizzle of olive oil, fresh chopped cilantro or mint, and a lemon wedge on the side.

## Tips for the Best Adas Soup

*   **Don't Skimp on the Lemon:** The fresh lemon juice is non-negotiable! It brightens the entire soup and provides a crucial tangy balance to the earthy lentils. Add it at the end to preserve its fresh flavor.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** A good extra virgin olive oil makes a noticeable difference, especially when used for sautéing and as a finishing drizzle.
*   **Proper Simmering:** Allow the lentils enough time to break down completely. This is key to achieving the creamy, comforting texture of authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning is personal. Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, and cumin. Sometimes a little more salt or a touch more cumin can elevate the flavors significantly.
*   **Fresh Herbs for Garnish:** While optional, fresh cilantro or mint truly elevates the soup’s aroma and visual appeal.

## Serving Suggestions for Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **With Pita Bread:** A classic pairing! Serve with warm, fresh pita bread for dipping, or toasted pita wedges. Some even fry small pieces of pita until crispy for a delightful textural contrast.
*   **As a Light Meal:** A bowl of Adas with a side of fresh vegetables or a simple salad (like a quick cucumber and tomato salad with a lemon-mint dressing) makes for a wholesome and satisfying light lunch or dinner.
*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve smaller portions as a starter to a larger Middle Eastern feast, perhaps alongside dishes like hummus, baba ghanoush, or tabbouleh.
*   **Garnish Generously:** Beyond fresh herbs and olive oil, consider a sprinkle of sumac for extra tang, or a pinch of Aleppo pepper for mild heat and beautiful color.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas recipe is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment:

*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrition and flavor, consider adding finely diced carrots or celery along with the onion at the beginning. A handful of fresh spinach or Swiss chard can also be stirred in during the last few minutes of cooking.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of turmeric can add a lovely golden hue and subtle earthy notes. A tiny bit of cayenne pepper or a few red pepper flakes can introduce a gentle heat. Ground coriander also pairs beautifully with cumin.
*   **Different Herbs:** While cilantro and mint are traditional, fresh parsley can also be used as a garnish.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A tiny hint of smoked paprika can add a unique depth, though it deviates slightly from the traditional bright flavor profile.
*   **Lentil Type:** While red lentils are ideal for their quick cooking and ability to create a creamy texture, brown or green lentils can be used, but they will take longer to cook and won't break down as much, resulting in a chunkier soup.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas vegan?**
Yes, traditionally it is! As long as you use vegetable broth or water, and no animal products, this soup is naturally vegan.

**Can I make this soup ahead of time?**
Absolutely! Like many soups, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

**Can I freeze Adas soup?**
Yes, it freezes beautifully. Allow the soup to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if it's too thick.

**Why is my lentil soup bland?**
The most common reasons for bland lentil soup are insufficient salt, not enough lemon juice, or a lack of cumin. Taste and adjust these key ingredients generously until the flavor pops!

**Do I need to soak red lentils before cooking?**
No, red lentils cook very quickly and do not require soaking. A good rinse is all that's needed.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is more than just a dish; it's a culinary hug, a nutritious powerhouse, and a testament to the simple yet profound flavors of Lebanese cuisine. Easy to prepare, incredibly satisfying, and bursting with vibrant tastes, this soup is a must-try for anyone looking to explore the rich world of Middle Eastern Soups and Stews. Give it a try, and you might just find your new favorite comfort food.
